items.title: Call to Order
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman called the meeting to order at 9:00 a.m. The purpose of this meeting was to provide information related to A Better Tent City.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman provided a land acknowledgement.

items.title: Jeff Willmer, Board Chair, A Better Tent City
notes:
J. Willmer spoke in favour of the recommendation in CSD-HOU-26-003 and expressed appreciation for the work put into finding a path to keep A Better Tent City operating following the dissolution of the Board of Directors.

J. Wilmer clarified that A Better Tent City reached out to the Region for support, and the Region reached out to the Working Centre.

In response to Council, J. Wilmer stated that he does not recall ever applying for operating funding from the federal or provincial government, but the Ontario Trillium Fund did provide funds some of the belonging and inclusion programs on site.

Responding to Council, J. Wilmer stated the gender breakdown at A Better Tent City us approximately 50% male-identifying and 50% female-identifying.

items.title: Acer Bonaparte, Kitchener
notes: A. Bonaparte spoke in opposition to the recommended motion in CSD-HOU-26-003, citing poor experiences in the past with shelters managed by the Working Centre. A. Bonaparte asked Council to consider allowing a different organization to support A Better Tent City.

items.title: Julian Ichim, Kitchener
notes: J. Ichim spoke in opposition to the proposed changes to A Better Tent City’s rules of operation, and discussed his lived experiences with homelessness.

items.title: Meagan Snyder, Kitchener
notes: M. Snyder spoke regarding concerns over the process surrounding the dissolution of A Better Tent City. M. Snyder emphasized the importance of the sense of community established by A Better Tent City for unhoused individuals.

items.title: Lake Trefler, Kitchener
notes: L. Trefler spoke regarding concerns expressed by residents of A Better Tent City and emphasized the importance of listening to vulnerable communities in Waterloo Region.

items.title: Lily Fozard, Waterloo
notes: L. Fozard spoke in opposition to the recommended motion in CSD-HOU-26-003 and emphasized the importance of community for those living unhoused within the Region.

items.title: Lynn Intini, Kitchener
notes: L. Intini spoke in opposition to the proposed motion in CSD-HOU-26-003 and emphasized the importance of creating a shelter system that allows residents to exercise autonomy.

items.title: Shannon Montgomery, Kitchener
notes: S. Montgomery spoke about the importance of community at A Better Tent City and expressed their desire for the same staff and volunteers to continue working there as A Better Tent City transitions.

items.title: Nadine Green, Kitchener
notes: N. Green spoke on her experience as a co-founder of A Better Tent City and her experiences living and working in this community. N. Green asked Council to allow her to keep living and working at A Better Tent City, to permit visitors, and to manage the transition of A Better Tent City in a manner that reflects its original purpose.

items.title: CSD-HOU-26-003, A Better Tent City Transition and Stabilization Plan
notes:
Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, introduced the report and acknowledged the complexity of the situation of the individuals affected.

P. Sweeney emphasized that two (2) streams of funding are being requested, one (1) for direct operational support and the other to support impacted individuals in the community. He emphasized that the transition does come with operational risks and that a significant financial investment is required.

Council raised concerns over the significant funding needed to operate A Better Tent City, and the lack of services available in Cambridge. Council emphasized that equity includes geographic equity, noting that it may not be possible for those living within the Region to visit a different city to seek services.

In response to Council, P. Sweeney noted that a proportional response is necessary for the 55 individuals residing at A Better Tent City and the 25-40 individuals that frequent the site for services. He stated staff have put forward a recommendation that reflects the true investments required to transition A Better Tent City. P. Sweeney noted that supports are required for individuals no longer staying at A Better Tent City, and resources will follow individuals to greatest extent possible.

P. Sweeney acknowledged that the investments proposed today may need to be offset by other reductions in the future. P. Sweeney advised against reducing the budget proposed in the report, as it would be too risky to commit to serving the needs of the population at A Better Tent City with fewer resources that what has been identified.

Council discussed options to bring forward a motion to direct funding to existing services in Cambridge.

Responding to a question from Council, P. Sweeney explained that of the requested $5.76 million total operating investment, only $2.9 million will be specifically for operations at the existing A Better Tent City, and the remaining resources would be used for community-based investments to support individuals who may no longer be able to reside there.

In response to Council, P. Sweeney indicated that staff could take direction and come back with an equity impact assessment and data regarding investments in Cambridge.

In response to Council, P. Sweeney clarified that A Better Tent City was previously operating outside of the formal organizational system, and that A Better Tent City leadership approached the Region. He further clarified that after A Better Tent City's transition into the housing stability system, the Region would act as the service system manager and will be required to meet legislated requirements. He also clarified that hiring is not handled by the Region, but there are certain expectations for operation and outcomes.

P. Sweeney explained that if the Region does not go forward with this, the responsibility would lie with A Better Tent City's current leadership board to wind down and the property use would be determined by its current owners, the Waterloo District School Board and the City of Kitchener.

Council acknowledged the hard work that will be required and emphasized need for accountability of transition plan

In response to Council, Ryan Pettipiere, Director, Housing Services, confirmed that funding would be used for net new spaces to support the transition and to create additional spaces in supportive housing, overnight warming/cooling spaces, and motel rooms.

Council expressed concerns related to the cost and operating funding and the impact this could have on the 2027 budget.

Responding to Council, P. Sweeney confirmed that staff clarify with funding partners that funding is subject to budget approval.

In response to Council, R. Pettipiere confirmed that if the recommended motion is passed, staff will proceed as outlined in the report. R. Pettipiere further confirmed that the cautions around accountability and future year budgets are part of a regular process for the Region and providers that occur year-to-year already.

Responding to Council, P. Sweeney confirmed staff have existing reporting mechanisms that get brought back to Council on a regular basis as business-as-usual.

Council discussed the need to invest in permanent supportive housing.

R. Pettipiere confirmed the cost to construct new supportive housing is approximating $300,000 per unit.

Responding to Council, P. Sweeney stated the Region would be legally responsible for the site, and subject to regulatory requirements surrounding health and safety. He stated that staff would not recommend reducing the funding provided for this project for this reason.

In response to Council, P. Sweeney confirmed that this report is consistent with the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness.

Council discussed the best way to move forward in a cost-effective way with the transition of A Better Tent City and support the individuals that currently live there.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-26-003, A Better Tent City Transition and Stabilization Plan
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo: Approve the A Better Tent City Stabilization and Transition Plan, including related funding, as outlined in report CSD-HOU-26-003, dated June 24, 2026. Amend the 2025 Housing Services Capital program to add $2.50M financed through reserves; Increase the 2026 Operating Budget for Housing Services in the amount of $2.56M, $0 regional levy impact, financed through reserves; and Approve the addition of one Support Worker and two Program Analysts positions in 2026 to provide housing support And that staff report to the Community and Health Services Committee as part of regular update reports on The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness on the status of the A Better Tent City Transition and Stabilization Plan, including; actual operating and capital expenditures to date; the number of ABTC residents assessed and connected to individualized housing plans; the number of residents transitioned into permanent, supportive, or alternative housing options; site safety, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance updates; performance measures for The Working Centre operating agreement; options to reduce or offset the 2027 levy impact, including provincial, federal, philanthropic, and community partner funding; and confirmation that any 2027 funding request will be considered through the regular 2027 budget process and not treated as automatic ongoing base funding without Council approval.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo:

  1. Approve the A Better Tent City Stabilization and Transition Plan, including related funding, as outlined in report CSD-HOU-26-003, dated June 24, 2026.
  2. Amend the 2025 Housing Services Capital program to add $2.50M financed through reserves;
  3. Increase the 2026 Operating Budget for Housing Services in the amount of $2.56M, $0 regional levy impact, financed through reserves; and
  4. Approve the addition of one Support Worker and two Program Analysts positions in 2026 to provide housing support

And that staff report to the Community and Health Services Committee as part of regular update reports on The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness on the status of the A Better Tent City Transition and Stabilization Plan, including;

  1. actual operating and capital expenditures to date;
  2. the number of ABTC residents assessed and connected to individualized housing plans;
  3. the number of residents transitioned into permanent, supportive, or alternative housing options;
  4. site safety, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance updates;
  5. performance measures for The Working Centre operating agreement;
  6. options to reduce or offset the 2027 levy impact, including provincial, federal, philanthropic, and community partner funding; and
  7. confirmation that any 2027 funding request will be considered through the regular 2027 budget process and not treated as automatic ongoing base funding without Council approval.
